SMTO-CFG-0004 — The Gateway can't start because its port number is invalid

GUID: 17ca0dce-6338-4182-9fd4-3a36c02fd50a
Slug: gateway-config-gateway-bind-port-must-be-between-1
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • The Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer) was given a network port number outside 1 to 65535, so it stopped before starting. Nothing ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the computer running the Gateway, check how it is started. If the start command includes --port (-Port on Windows), change the number to one from 1 to 65535, or remove it to use 8787. The --port option sets where the Gateway listens, and 0, negative numbers or numbers above 65535 aren't valid ports.
  2. If no --port is used, ask the person who set up that computer to correct the GATEWAY_BIND_PORT setting the same way. That setting supplies the port when the start command doesn't.
  3. If the port changed, open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Edit for that Gateway, enter the same number in Port, and select Save changes. SMTO connects to the Gateway on the port saved there, so both numbers must match.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway starts, and Check connection in Settings › Setup › Gateways shows it as Connected.

If it still fails

  • Send the Gateway's startup message, or the copied error details, to the person who installed the Gateway. Don't keep restarting it with the same setting; it will stop the same way each time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway Settings validation rejected GATEWAY_BIND_PORT (bind_port) because it is not in the range 1 to 65535, so the Gateway did not start.

What this means

  • Gateway settings validation finds bind_port at or below zero or above 65535 before service startup. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Gateway settings validation finds bind_port at or below zero or above 65535 before service startup.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect GATEWAY_BIND_PORT on the Gateway host, distinct from its outbound controller port.

How to fix it

  • Set GATEWAY_BIND_PORT (or the startup --port option, or bind_port in the Gateway instance's configuration/managed.json) to an unused port from 1 to 65535 (default 8787), restart the Gateway, and update the matching Gateway record's Port on the Server. This is the inbound listener port, separate from GATEWAY_SERVER_PORT.
  • Set GATEWAY_BIND_PORT to the intended port from 1 through 65535 and restart safely through its service controls.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Startup accepts the intended listening port in 1–65535.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
